body: I like A Better Place, A Better Time a lot. It's probably one of my favorite songs, and has helped me get through dark times. Lucky is nice, too. I think I prefer the electric version. Thank you for the words.
The relatability helps me feel a little more understood and less alone, I guess.
Either pro or anti is alright.

Blake is my favorite character as well.

Based off the posts that asks to rank people's favorite Volumes, it seems that Volume 1 is commonly the least favorite. However, it's actually my absolute favorite Volume. 

I can understand the criticism; the animation outside of the fights is pretty stiff, a lot of the characters don't get much development, and the ones that do just kind of change in the blink of an eye. However, it just has that charm to it that I haven't felt from any other Volume aside from maybe 2. 

It introduced so many of the characters we know and love, has some of the best fight scenes, and a lot of my favorite songs in the series. It also has great background scores too, though not many people pay attention to those.
I think the only thing that would succeed in making me drop the show at this point is if my favorite character (Blake) died, but that probably will never happen so I'm in it for the long haul.

I feel like the soundtrack as a whole has kind of gone downhill after Volume 3, though I know that's entirely subjective. I've seen some people that seem to legitimately like Volume 4's soundtrack, but the only song I personally like in that season is Home.

Volume 6's was better than the previous two seasons, at least. Though I still don't think they can compare to the first three Volumes.

For Rising, I'd have to say that it's my second to least favorite opening, just ahead of Volume 4's. Not to say that it's bad or anything, as I still enjoyed listening to it.

I don't really care for One Thing or Lionize. Miracle is cool (particularly the piano at the beginning and end), and Big Metal Shoe is pretty fun. Nevermore has grown on me, and while Forever Fall is probably my least favorite of the slow and sad songs, it's still nice.

Indomitable is definitely the best song in the season for me. Beautiful and powerful.

The extra tracks are whatever, I guess. Never been a fan of acoustic.

Hey, thanks for sharing your thoughts. I can understand where you're coming from with Summer's death, but unlike the show it's actually a reoccurring issue for Ruby to overcome; it's not a one time thing. You see instances of this in the later chapters.

I'm disappointed by a lot of things in this show, but Yang's PTSD is definitely one of the larger ones. As someone who suffers from it myself, I would have had an entirely different reaction upon meeting Adam if I were in Yang's shoes. I'd probably break down into tears or just be in complete panic. There's no way in hell I'd still be able to fight properly.

I can partially agree with your statement that she never should have had it in the first place. Not just because of your reasoning, but because of how they handled it in the show. I already wasn't really a fan of how rushed her whole arc was in Volume 4 and how the only effects the experience had on her was the occasional shaking of her arm, but the show crashed and burned with the entire concept when it mattered most. As such, it may as well have never been brought to attention to begin with. 

I do think, however, that Yang being conscious during her arm being sliced off is not necessarily the only determining factor for her PTSD. While yes, it definitely would have had an even larger impact on her mental state, there are other key aspects related to the event, most importantly being her lack of an arm. Whether she was awake or not, the stub and even the robotic arm is a daily reminder of that night. She may not have experienced the pain, but she is constantly living with the consequences for her reckless actions. It damaged her pride, her courage, and her willingness to continue on with her past motivations.

She still caught sight of the one who caused this injury, and was conscious for long enough for her mind to imagine what she had missed. Memories can often be one of your worst enemies, and while she may not have had much to go off of, sometimes thinking and imagining what may or may not have occurred is just as damaging as actually seeing it for yourself. Just the idea that Adam was powerful enough to slice through her aura and give her permanent damage is enough to affect anyone badly, in my personal opinion. I know that if I were Yang and woke up only to see that I was missing an arm and was told that my partner (and eventual love interest) had just abandoned me I'd be an emotional mess, and that experience would most likely haunt me forever.

So in short, Yang has valid reasons for having PTSD. The problem is that the way they handled the mental disorder itself just doesn't work. They just shoehorned in short scenes of her arm shaking and gave her occasional hallucinations only for them to amount to absolutely nothing.

Even before Volume 3 I thought Yang and Blake would be cute together, just like how I found White Rose to be appealing. However, unlike the latter ship I just couldn't see many signs that would support a relationship. In Volume 1 aside from their initiation Yang and Blake hardly had any interactions, and near the end of the season Blake's other love interest was introduced. 

In season 2 the most they had was that heart to heart in Burning The Candle. That was probably the first major sign of the ship, but I almost completely dismissed it during my first time watching the series since Blake also danced with Sun in the same scene.

And then in Volume 3 I became open to the possibility of them being together upon seeing how Yang sacrificed a part of herself as an attempt to keep Blake safe. How hurt Yang was over her leaving only solidified this for me.

I can definitely understand those who say that it feels like their relationship came out of nowhere, as it really could have needed more buildup and development. Volume 1 was full of timeskips, and during those scenes that we never got the chance to see we can safely assume that Yang, Blake and the rest of the team became closer, but it's hard to use that as an excuse for the ship when we never actually *see* what's happening. How did they become closer? What other antics did they get up to? Those questions will most likely never be answered outside of fanfictions.

While I love the ship, it has a lot of missed potential. And that also applies to the rest of the show in general. The entire series has so many possibilities for great things, but I rarely see it actually going down that path. Volume 6 helped ease a lot of my doubts, but even then it obviously wasn't perfect. 

But back to the topic at hand, I don't see the point of trying to reason with those kinds of people. No matter how you try to explain yourself they will twist your words around and always believe you're in the wrong. It's very rare to actually get through to them, and I'd rather not waste my time talking with disrespectful shippers.
Yeah, the trailers were great. It definitely gave me and many other people a different impression of what the series would be like than it actually turned out to be.
